content:
We have a target molecule: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. The guidance says Diels-Alder reaction is forward. So retrosynthesis: break the Diels-Alder to give diene and dienophile. The template 1914385 appears to be a Diels-Alder retro template: product (target) -> diene + dienophile. The template's retro direction: product >> diene + dienophile. The template's retro_smarts_template shows product to reactants: left side is product pattern, right side is two fragments: a diene (CH2=CH-CH=CH2) and a dienophile (methyl ester? Actually the right side shows [C;D1;H3:1]-[#8:2]-[C:3](=[O;...])-[C;H0;D3;+0:5]1=[CH;...]-[C:7](=[O...])-[C:9]-1 which is a cyclic product? Wait the right side is two fragments: a diene fragment and a dienophile fragment. The product is a bicyclic lactone? The target is a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone? Let's examine target: COC(=O) attached to a chiral carbon bridging two rings? Actually SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. That's methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe a bicyclo[2.2.1]?). The Diels-Alder retro would give a diene (maybe cyclopentadiene?) and a dienophile (maybe methyl acrylate). The template likely splits into a diene fragment: [CH2:10]=[CH:11]-[CH:12]=[CH2:13] (a 1,3-butadiene) and a dienophile fragment: methyl ester attached to a carbonyl and a double bond? Actually the dienophile is a carbonyl with a double bond? The right side of template: [C;D1;H3:1]-[#8:2]-[C:3](=[O;...])-[C;H0;D3;+0:5]1=[CH;...]-[C:7](=[O...])-[C:9]-1. That looks like a cyclic enone? Hmm.

But we have the template ID 1914385, which matches our target. So we can use that template for retrosynthesis. We need to produce a JSON route: root molecule is target, child is reaction with template_id 1914385, children are precursor molecules (two). We need to get the precursor SMILES from the template application. We can apply the template to get precursors using apply_template.
